traceability.evidence:
Implementation and tests for docs/stories/010.0-DEV-DEEP-VALIDATION.story.md are present and passing.
Key implementation: - Rule file: src/rules/valid-req-reference.ts - Header references this story and its requirements: - "@story docs/stories/010.0-DEV-DEEP-VALIDATION.story.md" - "@req REQ-DEEP-PARSE - Parse comments and extract story/requirement metadata" - "@req REQ-DEEP-MATCH - Match @req annotations to story file requirements" - "@req REQ-DEEP-CACHE - Cache requirement IDs per story file for efficient validation" - Core behavior: - loadAndCacheRequirements(): reads story file once, extracts all requirement IDs with regex /REQ-[A-Z0-9-]+/g and caches them in a Map<string, Set> (REQ-DEEP-PARSE, REQ-DEEP-CACHE). - checkRequirementExists(): checks if a referenced reqId is in the cached Set and reports messageId "reqMissing" with both reqId and storyPath when not found (REQ-DEEP-MATCH, REQ-DEEP-ERROR). - validateAndResolveStoryPath(): validates storyPath against path traversal and absolutes, resolving relative to cwd and reporting "invalidPath" when unsafe (integration with existing path rules, plus robust path checking). - validateReqLine() and handleAnnotationLine()/processAllComments(): parse @story / @req lines from all comments and drive the deep validation, integrating with existing annotation styles (same @story/@req syntax as 005.0 & 006.0). - validateImplementsLine()/parseImplementsLine(): support @implements annotations with a story path and multiple requirement IDs, using the same caching and checking pipeline (integration with 010.2 multi-story behavior). - programListener(): wires this into ESLint’s Program visitor, maintaining a per-file cache of requirements. - Error messages: - reqMissing: "Requirement '{{reqId}}' not found in '{{storyPath}}'" with JSDoc tying it to 010.0 and 007.0 (clear, requirement-specific diagnostics). - invalidPath: "Invalid story path '{{storyPath}}'" also documented against 010.0 & 007.0. - Error handling: - loadAndCacheRequirements() wraps fs.readFileSync in try/catch and, on any filesystem error (malformed/unreadable/missing file), safely records an empty Set instead of throwing, ensuring the rule degrades to clean "reqMissing" diagnostics rather than crashing.
Tests specifically for this story: - File: tests/rules/valid-req-reference.test.ts - Header explicitly ties tests to the story and its requirements: - "Tests for: docs/stories/010.0-DEV-DEEP-VALIDATION.story.md" - "@story docs/stories/010.0-DEV-DEEP-VALIDATION.story.md" - "@req REQ-DEEP-PARSE - Verify valid-req-reference rule enforces existing requirement content" - Valid cases: - "[REQ-DEEP-PARSE] valid requirement reference existing in story file" using: // @story docs/stories/001.0-DEV-PLUGIN-SETUP.story.md // @req REQ-PLUGIN-STRUCTURE Confirms deep validation succeeds when the requirement exists. - "[REQ-DEEP-BULLET] valid bullet list requirement existing in bullet story fixture" using: // @story tests/fixtures/story_bullet.md // @req REQ-BULLET-LIST with tests/fixtures/story_bullet.md containing bullet-list requirements: - REQ-BULLET-LIST - a requirement in bullet list format - REQ-ANOTHER - another requirement This demonstrates support for non-trivial story file structure and bullet format (REQ-DEEP-FORMAT, REQ-DEEP-SECTION). - "[REQ-DEEP-IMPLEMENTS] single implements line with multiple requirements in multi-story fixture" and "[REQ-DEEP-IMPLEMENTS] multi-story implements with shared requirement IDs" using story_multi_a.md and story_multi_b.md, each containing: - REQ-SHARED-ID - REQ-ONLY-A / REQ-ONLY-B Confirms @implements with multiple requirement IDs and multi-story scenarios are deep-validated. - Invalid cases: - "[REQ-DEEP-MATCH] missing requirement in story file" expects messageId "reqMissing" with specific data { reqId: "REQ-NON-EXISTENT", storyPath: "docs/stories/001.0-DEV-PLUGIN-SETUP.story.md" }. - Path security / parsing validation: - Disallow path traversal in story path and implements story path (messageId "invalidPath"). - Disallow absolute paths in story path (messageId "invalidPath"). - "[REQ-DEEP-BULLET] missing bullet list requirement in bullet story fixture" validates error behavior for bullet-based stories. - "[REQ-DEEP-IMPLEMENTS] missing implements requirement in multi-story fixture" validates deep matching for @implements.
Documentation for deep validation behavior: - File: docs/rules/valid-req-reference.md - Annotated with this story: - "@story docs/stories/010.0-DEV-DEEP-VALIDATION.story.md" - "@req REQ-DEEP-PARSE - Parse story files to extract requirement identifiers" - "@req REQ-DEEP-MATCH - Validate `@req` references against story file content" - "@req REQ-DEEP-PATH - Protect against path traversal in story paths" - Describes behavior in terms of this story's goals: - Validates that @req and @implements reference existing requirements in story files. - Explains path validation (invalidPath), deep content parsing (REQ tokens from the file), and error conditions (reqMissing). - Provides multiple examples for correct and incorrect usage (single-story, multi-story, bullet-like formats, @implements, path traversal, and absolute-path errors). - Explicitly discusses interaction of @story/@req and @implements and how each is validated against story content, matching the multi-format, multi-structure requirements in the story.
Supporting fixtures for format & structure: - tests/fixtures/story_bullet.md: requirements in a bullet list under a "## Requirements" section. - tests/fixtures/story_multi_a.md and story_multi_b.md: multi-story fixtures with shared and distinct IDs, demonstrating that requirement IDs are treated as scoped to each story file and showing the rule works with realistic markdown structures.
Test execution evidence: - Command run: npm test -- --verbose - Jest suite includes: "Valid Req Reference Rule (Story 010.0-DEV-DEEP-VALIDATION)". - Output (excerpt): - PASS tests/rules/valid-req-reference.test.ts - valid ✓ [REQ-DEEP-PARSE] valid requirement reference existing in story file (8 ms) ✓ [REQ-DEEP-BULLET] valid bullet list requirement existing in bullet story fixture (2 ms) ✓ [REQ-DEEP-IMPLEMENTS] single implements line with multiple requirements in multi-story fixture (1 ms) ✓ [REQ-DEEP-IMPLEMENTS] multi-story implements with shared requirement IDs (7 ms) - invalid ✓ [REQ-DEEP-MATCH] missing requirement in story file (1 ms) ✓ [REQ-DEEP-PARSE] disallow path traversal in story path (1 ms) ✓ [REQ-DEEP-PARSE] disallow absolute path in story path (6 ms) ✓ [REQ-DEEP-BULLET] missing bullet list requirement in bullet story fixture (1 ms) ✓ [REQ-DEEP-IMPLEMENTS] missing implements requirement in multi-story fixture (1 ms) ✓ [REQ-DEEP-IMPLEMENTS] disallow path traversal in implements story path (1 ms) - Global test summary: - Test Suites: 35 passed, 35 total - Tests: 266 passed, 266 total
Acceptance criteria coverage: - Core Functionality: Implemented via deep parsing (regex over full story content) and checkRequirementExists; verified by valid and invalid tests for existing and missing requirements in real story files. - Quality Standards (formats & structures): The rule treats story files as arbitrary markdown text and extracts REQ-* identifiers regardless of section or list structure, demonstrated via the standard story file, bullet-list fixture, and multi-story fixtures. This satisfies handling of various structures and list styles called out in the story. - Integration: The rule uses the same annotation conventions (@story, @req, @implements) as earlier stories and coexists with valid-annotation-format and valid-story-reference. It safely validates paths and content without conflicting with those rules, and is enabled through the plugin’s configs (see docs/rules/valid-req-reference.md and passing plugin/config tests). - User Experience: Error messages are explicit and tested: "Requirement '{{reqId}}' not found in '{{storyPath}}'" and "Invalid story path '{{storyPath}}'", with tests asserting correct messageIds and data payloads. - Error Handling: fs.readFileSync is wrapped in a try/catch to avoid crashes on unreadable/malformed/missing story files, and the rule falls back to an empty requirement set, producing consistent reqMissing diagnostics instead of runtime errors. Path traversal and absolute path issues are handled via explicit invalidPath diagnostics. - Documentation: docs/rules/valid-req-reference.md documents the deep validation behavior, supported usage patterns, error modes, and examples that match the story’s described behavior.
All related tests pass in the full suite, providing concrete verification that the implementation satisfies the behavior described in docs/stories/010.0-DEV-DEEP-VALIDATION.story.md.
traceability.notes: The valid-req-reference ESLint rule, its tests, and its documentation together implement the deep requirement content validation described in story 010.0-DEV-DEEP-VALIDATION. It parses story files to extract REQ identifiers, caches them, validates both @req and @implements annotations against those identifiers, enforces safe paths, and reports clear, requirement-specific errors. Tests explicitly tie to this story and cover success and failure cases, including bullet-list and multi-story scenarios. Documentation explains the behavior and supported patterns. All tests pass, so this story is fully implemented.
